sentences: He talks a big game but rarely follows through on promises.
He followed through the hallway during the office tour.
I followed through the park during the guided nature walk.
She followed through the door behind her colleague today.
explanation: 'follow through' (commitments) = complete. Not following physically.
explanationJa: 「follow through」は「最後までやり通す」。物理的に追う意味ではない。

sentences: He came around the back of the house through the garden.
She came around the corner of the office building today.
I came around the side of the parked truck slowly.
She wasn't sure at first, but she came around to the idea.
explanation: 'come around' (opinions) = agree eventually. Not physical movement.
explanationJa: 「come around」は「考えを変えて同意する」。回り込む意味ではない。

sentences: Light dawned on the lake during the peaceful morning.
The morning dawned on the campsite during our trip.
The sun dawned on the mountains during the early hike.
It just dawned on me that I forgot to send the invoice.
explanation: 'dawn on' (realization) = suddenly realize. Not actual dawn.
explanationJa: 「dawn on」は「ハッと気づく」。実際の夜明けの意味ではない。

sentences: He leaned toward the doorway during the long conversation.
She leaned toward the wall while taking the family photo.
I leaned toward the bookshelf to reach the top shelf.
I'm leaning toward the second candidate for this role.
explanation: 'lean toward' (preferences) = prefer. Not physical leaning.
explanationJa: 「lean toward」は「~の方に傾く(好み)」。物理的に傾く意味ではない。

sentences: She minded you carefully during the daycare shift today.
I minded you at the kindergarten this whole afternoon.
He minded you in the playground while the parents talked.
It's a great deal — mind you, the warranty is limited.
explanation: 'mind you' = note that (idiom). Not 'taking care of you'.
explanationJa: 「mind you」は「ただし~だけど」。「あなたの世話をする」意味ではない。

sentences: Granted, the price is high, but the quality justifies it.
He granted the loan to the qualified applicant today.
She granted the wish for her birthday this year.
I granted permission for the field trip to the museum.
explanation: 'granted' (concession) = admittedly. Not 'giving' meaning.
explanationJa: 「granted」(譲歩)は「確かに」。「与える」意味ではない。

sentences: I that said my opinion at the parent teacher conference.
It's a great phone. That said, the battery life isn't ideal.
She that said her speech at the wedding reception.
He that said his lines on the theater stage perfectly.
explanation: 'that said' = however (transition phrase). Not a verb construction.
explanationJa: 「that said」は「とはいえ」(つなぎ表現)。動詞句ではない。

sentences: She came to think of it across the wide open meadow today.
He came to think of it under the bridge while waiting.
I came to think of it through the long quiet hallway.
Come to think of it, I haven't seen Mark since last summer.
explanation: 'come to think of it' = now realizing. Not physical motion.
explanationJa: 「come to think of it」は「そう言えば」。物理的な動きではない。

sentences: On second thought, let's just order delivery instead.
He drew on second thought across the canvas yesterday.
I painted on second thought onto the bedroom wall.
She wrote on second thought in her diary every evening.
explanation: 'on second thought' = reconsidering. Not writing surfaces.
explanationJa: 「on second thought」は「やっぱり」。書く場所の意味ではない。

sentences: All things considered, the trip was a real success.
He stacked all things considered on the storage shelf.
I arranged all things considered into the moving truck.
She put all things considered onto the kitchen table.
explanation: 'all things considered' = overall. Not physical things.
explanationJa: 「all things considered」は「全てを考慮すると」。物の意味ではない。

sentences: She scored a fair point during the basketball game.
I gained a fair point during the volleyball tournament.
Fair point — I hadn't thought about it from that angle.
He earned a fair point in the tennis match yesterday.
explanation: 'fair point' = valid argument. Not a sports point.
explanationJa: 「fair point」は「もっともな指摘」。スポーツの得点ではない。

sentences: I point taken the test in school this morning quickly.
Point taken — I'll be more careful with my deadlines.
She point taken the photo of the family during dinner.
He point taken the ball into the basketball hoop.
explanation: 'point taken' = I accept your argument. Not a verb construction.
explanationJa: 「point taken」は「了解した、納得」。動詞句ではない。

sentences: I beg to differ — the data actually shows the opposite trend.
She begged to differ for some money on the street corner.
He begged to differ for food outside the restaurant.
I begged to differ for shelter during the heavy rainstorm.
explanation: 'beg to differ' = politely disagree (idiom). Not literal begging.
explanationJa: 「beg to differ」は「失礼ながら反対する」。物乞いの意味ではない。

sentences: She has a point on top of her sharpened pencil today.
He has a point on his fishing hook for tomorrow's trip.
I have a point on the end of my new sewing needle.
You have a point — maybe we should reconsider this approach.
explanation: 'have a point' (arguments) = valid argument. Not literal points.
explanationJa: 「have a point」は「言い分にも一理ある」。物の先端の意味ではない。

sentences: I traded it for what it's worth at the consignment shop.
He bought it for what it's worth at the antique store.
She sold it for what it's worth at the garage sale.
For what it's worth, I think you made the right call.
explanation: 'for what it's worth' (opinion) = humbly offered. Not actual value.
explanationJa: 「for what it's worth」は「参考までに」。実際の価値の意味ではない。

sentences: He kept it needless to say in the meditation studio today.
Needless to say, the project deadline is non-negotiable.
She found it needless to say at the noisy quiet library.
I made it needless to say during the silent retreat.
explanation: 'needless to say' = obviously (transition). Not a verb action.
explanationJa: 「needless to say」は「言うまでもなく」。動詞ではない。

sentences: She solved as a matter of fact during the science experiment.
As a matter of fact, I just spoke with him this morning.
I researched as a matter of fact for my history assignment.
He proved as a matter of fact in the geometry problem set.
explanation: 'as a matter of fact' = in fact (transition). Not 'a fact'.
explanationJa: 「as a matter of fact」は「実は」。「事実」そのものではない。

sentences: I tripped when push comes to shove during the soccer match.
She started when push comes to shove during the rugby game.
He fell when push comes to shove during wrestling practice.
When push comes to shove, you can really count on her.
explanation: 'when push comes to shove' = at critical moment. Not physical pushing.
explanationJa: 「when push comes to shove」は「いざという時」。実際に押し合う意味ではない。

sentences: He shouted a far cry from across the canyon during the hike.
She made a far cry from the back of the auditorium today.
This new place is a far cry from our old apartment.
I let out a far cry from the top of the mountain peak.
explanation: 'a far cry from' = very different. Not literal crying out.
explanationJa: 「a far cry from」は「~とは大違い」。遠くで叫ぶ意味ではない。

word: at the end of the day
sentences: At the end of the day, what matters most is being healthy.
She felt tired at the end of the day after her shift.
He came home at the end of the day from the office.
I relaxed at the end of the day on my comfortable couch.
explanation: 'at the end of the day' (idiom) = ultimately. Not literal day's end.
explanationJa: 「at the end of the day」は「結局のところ」。一日の終わりの意味ではない。

sentences: I'll give him the benefit of the doubt on this one.
He claimed the benefit of the doubt on his tax return.
I applied for the benefit of the doubt at the welfare office.
She received the benefit of the doubt from her health insurance.
explanation: 'benefit of the doubt' = give trust (idiom). Not financial benefit.
explanationJa: 「benefit of the doubt」は「疑わしきは罰せず」。給付金の意味ではない。

sentences: If you read between the lines, she's clearly unhappy here.
I read between the lines of the printed graph paper.
He read between the lines of the lined exercise book.
She read between the lines on the ruled notebook paper today.
explanation: 'read between the lines' = infer (idiom). Not literal reading.
explanationJa: 「read between the lines」は「行間を読む」。実際に行間を読む意味ではない。

sentences: She crossed that bridge over the river during the morning hike.
I crossed that bridge near the train station this weekend.
He crossed that bridge in the city park yesterday afternoon.
We'll cross that bridge when we come to it next month.
explanation: 'cross that bridge' = deal with later (idiom). Not physical bridges.
explanationJa: 「cross that bridge」は「その時はその時」。実際の橋を渡る意味ではない。

sentences: Let me play devil's advocate here — what if we're wrong?
He played devil's advocate at the church theatrical performance.
I played devil's advocate in the school drama production.
She played devil's advocate on the courtroom stage during the play.
explanation: 'play devil's advocate' = argue opposite for discussion. Not acting role.
explanationJa: 「play devil's advocate」は「あえて反対意見を言う」。役を演じる意味ではない。

sentences: I received a tough call from the long distance number today.
Choosing between those two finalists was a tough call.
She made a tough call on her cell phone during the interview.
He answered a tough call at the busy customer service desk.
explanation: 'a tough call' = hard decision (idiom). Not a phone call.
explanationJa: 「a tough call」は「難しい判断」。電話の意味ではない。

sentences: He rowed in the same boat across the calm pond today.
I rode in the same boat on the river cruise yesterday.
We're all in the same boat with these new requirements.
She sat in the same boat during the lake fishing trip.
explanation: 'in the same boat' = same situation (idiom). Not actual boats.
explanationJa: 「in the same boat」は「同じ状況」。実際の船の意味ではない。

sentences: I parked by and large in the spacious parking lot today.
She worked by and large in the office supply storage room.
He stood by and large near the warehouse loading dock.
By and large, the team is happy with the new schedule.
explanation: 'by and large' = generally (idiom). Not a position descriptor.
explanationJa: 「by and large」は「概して」。位置の意味ではない。

sentences: I sold for the most part at the local farmers market.
She bought for the most part at the grocery store yesterday.
For the most part, the meeting went smoothly today.
He paid for the most part on his way out of the cafe.
explanation: 'for the most part' = mostly (transition). Not 'the largest part'.
explanationJa: 「for the most part」は「大部分は」(つなぎ)。実際の量の意味ではない。

sentences: The project is more or less done — just final edits remain.
He poured more or less into the empty glass at the table.
I added more or less to the recipe while baking yesterday.
She had more or less in the pitcher during dinner tonight.
explanation: 'more or less' = approximately (idiom). Not quantities of liquid.
explanationJa: 「more or less」は「だいたい」。液体の量の意味ではない。

sentences: He walked one way or another along the country road.
I cycled one way or another through the city streets.
She drove one way or another down the busy highway.
One way or another, we'll get this finished by Friday.
explanation: 'one way or another' = somehow (idiom). Not literal directions.
explanationJa: 「one way or another」は「何とかして」。方向の意味ではない。

sentences: I liked it or not the music at the concert last weekend.
He liked it or not the movie at the theater yesterday.
Like it or not, remote work is here to stay these days.
She liked it or not the food at the new restaurant tonight.
explanation: 'like it or not' = regardless (idiom). Not a verb construction.
explanationJa: 「like it or not」は「好むと好まざるとに関わらず」。動詞句ではない。

sentences: I prayed as luck would have it before the big competition.
She wished as luck would have it during her birthday wish.
He hoped as luck would have it before opening the lottery ticket.
As luck would have it, we ran into him at the airport.
explanation: 'as luck would have it' = by coincidence. Not 'wishing for luck'.
explanationJa: 「as luck would have it」は「運のいいことに」。幸運を願う意味ではない。

sentences: She told the truth be told to the police officer at the scene.
I shared the truth be told during the formal interview.
Truth be told, I wasn't a fan of the proposal either.
He spoke the truth be told on the witness stand in court.
explanation: 'truth be told' = honestly (idiom phrase). Not 'telling truth'.
explanationJa: 「truth be told」は「正直に言うと」。「真実を語る」意味ではない。

sentences: He gambled on the off chance during the football game.
She bet on the off chance at the casino last weekend.
I wagered on the off chance during the horse racing event.
On the off chance you see Sarah, please tell her I called.
explanation: 'on the off chance' = small possibility (idiom). Not gambling odds.
explanationJa: 「on the off chance」は「もしかしたら」。賭けの確率の意味ではない。

sentences: Odds are, the package will arrive sometime tomorrow afternoon.
He calculated the odds are at the casino blackjack table.
She bet the odds are on the lottery numbers this week.
I checked the odds are on the sports betting website today.
explanation: 'odds are' = likely (idiom). Not betting odds.
explanationJa: 「odds are」は「~の可能性が高い」。賭けのオッズの意味ではない。

word: as far as I can tell
sentences: She walked as far as I can tell down the long sidewalk.
As far as I can tell, the system is working correctly now.
He ran as far as I can tell on the marathon course route.
I biked as far as I can tell along the scenic mountain trail.
explanation: 'as far as I can tell' = to my knowledge (idiom). Not distance.
explanationJa: 「as far as I can tell」は「私の知る限り」。距離の意味ではない。

sentences: She gave it a shot of espresso at the morning meeting.
I gave it a shot of vaccine during the medical checkup.
He gave it a shot of vodka with the cocktail tonight.
Why not give it a shot? You've got nothing to lose, really.
explanation: 'give it a shot' = try (idiom). Not a measurement of liquid/medicine.
explanationJa: 「give it a shot」は「やってみる」。量や注射の意味ではない。

sentences: He's in hot water with the boss after missing the deadline.
I cooked in hot water during the pasta-making demonstration.
He soaked in hot water in the bathtub after a long workday.
She bathed in hot water at the spa during her relaxing weekend.
explanation: 'in hot water' = in trouble (idiom). Not literal hot water.
explanationJa: 「in hot water」は「困った状況」。実際のお湯の意味ではない。

sentences: Our office is just a stone's throw from the train station.
She did a stone's throw across the calm pond yesterday.
I attempted a stone's throw at the lake during the picnic.
He practiced a stone's throw at the river over the weekend.
explanation: 'a stone's throw' = nearby (idiom). Not literal throwing stones.
explanationJa: 「a stone's throw」は「目と鼻の先」。石を投げる意味ではない。

sentences: He explored second nature during the wilderness camping trip.
She studied second nature at the local botanical garden.
I photographed second nature in the forest preserve yesterday.
Driving stick is second nature to me after all these years.
explanation: 'second nature' = automatic skill (idiom). Not literal nature.
explanationJa: 「second nature」は「すっかり身についた」。自然の意味ではない。

sentences: It's not perfect, but it'll work in a pinch for tonight.
I noticed a small in a pinch on my arm from the bug bite.
She gave him in a pinch on the cheek to wake him up.
He felt a pain in a pinch from the tight new shoes.
explanation: 'in a pinch' = if needed (idiom). Not literal pinching.
explanationJa: 「in a pinch」は「いざという時」。つねる意味ではない。

sentences: I scored par for the course during my morning round of golf.
She shot par for the course during the golf tournament.
Late deliveries are pretty much par for the course with them.
He achieved par for the course at the country club tournament.
explanation: 'par for the course' = expected (idiom). Not literal golf score.
explanationJa: 「par for the course」は「お決まり/想定内」。ゴルフの得点の意味ではない。

sentences: He chose give or take in the gift exchange at the holiday party.
It'll take an hour, give or take, depending on traffic conditions.
She did give or take from the donation box at the charity event.
I selected give or take from the office supply closet today.
explanation: 'give or take' = approximately (idiom). Not give/take action.
explanationJa: 「give or take」は「だいたい」。「与える/受け取る」意味ではない。

sentences: She saw eye to eye in the optometrist's office during the exam.
He saw eye to eye through the new prescription glasses.
I saw eye to eye during the routine vision test today.
We don't always see eye to eye, but we work well together.
explanation: 'see eye to eye' = agree (idiom). Not literal eye contact.
explanationJa: 「see eye to eye」は「意見が合う」。実際の目の意味ではない。

sentences: I kept posted by the front door during the open house tour.
Keep me posted on how the negotiation goes tomorrow.
She kept posted at the front desk during her shift.
He kept posted near the building entrance during the event.
explanation: 'keep posted' = keep informed (idiom). Not standing as a guard.
explanationJa: 「keep posted」は「随時知らせて」。立ち番をする意味ではない。

sentences: Finishing this report by tomorrow is a tall order, honestly.
He requested a tall order at the fast food drive thru today.
She placed a tall order at the coffee shop this morning.
I made a tall order at the takeout restaurant for dinner.
explanation: 'a tall order' = difficult task (idiom). Not a beverage size.
explanationJa: 「a tall order」は「難題」。飲み物のサイズの意味ではない。

sentences: I noted the jury is still out at the legal proceedings yesterday.
She watched the jury is still out in the courtroom drama film.
The jury is still out on whether the new policy will work.
He observed the jury is still out during the murder trial.
explanation: 'the jury is still out' = undecided (idiom). Not a literal jury.
explanationJa: 「the jury is still out」は「まだ結論が出ていない」。実際の陪審員の意味ではない。
